html:
The Dâw are a small Amazonian people living on the Rio Negro near São Gabriel da Cachoeira, in the far northwest of Brazil. They speak a language of the Naduhup family, once called Makú, related to the languages of the Hup and Yuhup.

Like other Naduhup peoples, they were forest hunters and gatherers who traded game and forest goods with the farming, river-dwelling Tukanoan and Arawakan peoples around them, who often treated them as inferiors. In the 20th century traders, alcohol and disease brought them close to extinction before their numbers began to recover. They are one of the many peoples of the Amazon forest in Brazil.
